description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Checkov fixture whose failed checks include records whose path cannot be established. Every value was derived by reading the fixture, the recorded runner metadata and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, and every anchor fact was checked against the pinned tree at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d -- never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. It is the direct negative counterpart of AAP 0.5.3's first user example: the positive sibling proves the leading slash on file_path is honoured, and this file proves the file_abs_path reconciliation is a real check rather than decoration.
scanner_class_note: Fixed for this tool by AAP 0.5.4's class table and carried unchanged on every row. It does not vary with check_type, with the reporting framework or with record content; trivy is the single tool whose class is decided per record, from the section the record was read from. A rejected record carries no scanner_class at all, because it produces no row.

fixture.top_level_form_note: A single report object -- the form a Checkov artifact takes when one framework reports. The multi-framework array form is covered by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov-alt-shape.json and is not re-covered here: this fixture's subject is path resolution, and testing one thing at a time is what makes a failure attributable.
fixture.summary_note: The report's own summary object, quoted as the fixture carries it. It is never used as the record count: the count unit below is the one normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction. It happens to agree with that count here, and agreement is not the same as authority.
fixture.derived_from: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/checkov.json, itself an excerpt of harness/artifacts/raw/checkov.json (sha256 d5e4492ac799875f6cf14c187f9130bc2ad3f8060c320e757c127dfd1fda98fc, 6 failed checks)
fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. Two of the four failed checks are unmodified captured output: /results/failed_checks/0 is identical to the raw artifact's failed_checks[5] and to the positive fixture's failed_checks[4], and /results/failed_checks/1 is identical to the raw artifact's failed_checks[4] and the positive fixture's failed_checks[3]. The other two are the synthesized defective records, each derived from a captured record by changing its anchor fields and nothing else.
fixture.captured_provenance: Established by canonical-JSON comparison of every field of every record, not by eye. /results/failed_checks/2 agrees with the raw artifact's failed_checks[1] on 26 of its 28 fields, differing only in file_abs_path (the captured absolute path replaced by a file: URI naming a different file) and repo_file_path (nulled). /results/failed_checks/3 agrees with the raw artifact's failed_checks[3] on 26 of its 28 fields, differing only in those same two fields, both nulled. So in each case the sole defect is the record's statement about its own location -- check_id, check_name, severity, file_line_range, check_result and every other field are the tool's own output. That isolation is the point: a fixture that changed a second field could not attribute the rejection to the path.
fixture.sha256_purpose: The recorded digest is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible. These expectations are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- this artifact is not SARIF and routes to the native adapter keyed by the runner that wrote it. It carries no version of "2.1.0" and no runs array, which together are the whole of the SARIF test.
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("checkov", doc) returns tool "checkov", shape "checkov", adapter "checkov", scanner_class "misconfig"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No shape failure is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed Checkov report in its object form and routes cleanly; two records inside it are defective, and the adapter rejects those while still emitting the others. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. This fixture is eligible material for it, being native, but the assertion is that file's and is not restated here.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, of which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py carries the authored copy AAP 0.6.4's import restriction requires. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS -- so a record whose path cannot be resolved is rejected and counted rather than emitted with a null path.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations. That the runner also reads the allowlist to build its 18 -d target roots is a fact about its reach, not about this field.

resolution_context.worked_example: AAP 0.5.3's first user example, carried in unchanged. Checkov's file_path is relative to the scan target and carries a leading slash, alongside file_abs_path holding the filesystem-absolute path and repo_file_path a root-relative path that also carries a leading slash. The expected path is the leading slash stripped and the remainder treated as root-relative, reconciled against the absolute file_abs_path the same record carries. This fixture is the case where that reconciliation has something to catch.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the checkov entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.runner_invocation: one checkov invocation carrying 18 root-relative -d target roots, recorded at runner-metadata.json tools.checkov.invocation_form. This is the fact that makes file_path ambiguous on its own, and therefore the fact that makes an anchor field load-bearing rather than a convenience.
resolution_context.anchor_used: repo_file_path on both rows; neither rejected record has a usable anchor at all
resolution_context.anchor_rule: repo_file_path is root-relative and carries a leading slash, so exactly one slash is stripped and the remainder is the row's path. file_abs_path is filesystem-absolute and is relativized to the scan root. The branch is chosen by which field it is, never by whether the value looks absolute -- which is the whole of the worked example, since repo_file_path looks filesystem-absolute while not being it.
resolution_context.file_path_role: corroboration only. Under per_target_directory the slash-stripped file_path is relative to whichever -d root matched, so it corroborates by being a suffix of the anchored path -- and it is, on both rows. A disagreement is recorded rather than resolved and never suppresses a row; a file_path with no anchor beside it is not promoted to an anchor, which is what rejects /results/failed_checks/3.
resolution_context.why_file_path_alone_is_wrong: Stripping the slash off file_path and joining the remainder to the tree root names dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile, a directory that does not exist at the root and which matches no allowlist glob, so every row would silently take in_scope false. Reading the same value as filesystem-absolute is the failure the worked example warns about: it relativizes to a long ../ chain, with nothing crashing. No expected path in this file begins with / or contains a ../ segment.
resolution_context.scan_root_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, spark_src and the checkov entry's resolved_scan_root
resolution_context.root_independence: Both rows below hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given: each path comes from repo_file_path, which is already root-relative and needs no root to resolve. No row carries an absolute path in any field. The absolute values that do appear in this file are quoted evidence rather than emitted data -- the recorded scan root, each record's own anchor values under row_derivations and rejections, the parsing-error entry Checkov reported verbatim -- and none of them reaches a row. The first rejection is root-independent for its own reason: a file: URI names nothing expressible under any root, so no choice of root could make it resolve. The second is root-independent because the fault is a missing anchor, which no root supplies.
resolution_context.severity_source: the record's own severity field, which is null on every failed check because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is deliberately absent. severity.resolve then states the absence rather than assuming a level: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. No CVSS score is consulted -- a misconfiguration carries none, and AAP 0.5.4's checkov row names severity and nothing else.
resolution_context.start_line_source: file_line_range[0], as an integer. Both rejected records also carry a usable file_line_range, and neither is ever read: start_line is step 5 of the classification order and the path is step 4, so a record rejected on its path never reaches it.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve_source: the closed field set guideline, description, short_description, bc_category, benchmarks, details, vulnerability_details. Every one of them is null or an empty array on every record here, so no CWE or CVE token exists to collect and both fields are null on both rows. check_name is deliberately outside that set: it is the row's message, and harvesting an identifier out of a message would put a weakness reference in the dataset that the record never made as a reference.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on both rows. A misconfiguration names a location in a configuration file rather than a package, so no coordinate can be formed -- and that absence is not a rejection: AAP 0.5.4 attaches unformable_package_coordinate to a dependency-oriented record, which this is not.

rejection_boundary.statement: A path that cannot be established is a rejection. A path that merely resolves somewhere unwanted is a kept row with in_scope false. Both defective records here resolve to nothing that may be emitted, which is what makes them the unresolvable_path case rather than one of the kept cases below.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of only two never-absent fields in the twelve-field schema, the other being severity_norm: emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries path, and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate. A record with no resolvable path therefore has no valid row representation at all -- emit.validate_rows refuses a null path with the reason 'path and severity_norm are never absent: a record whose path could not be resolved was rejected and counted upstream' -- so counting it under a named class is the only outcome that neither drops the record nor invents a coordinate for it.
rejection_boundary.the_contradiction: This is the reasoning that makes the first rejection correct rather than merely defensible. Where the positive fixture carries a consistent triple -- every record's stripped file_path a suffix of a repo_file_path that agrees exactly with the relativized file_abs_path -- /results/failed_checks/2 carries two statements about its own location that cannot both be true. file_path says the finding is in dockerfiles/spark/bindings/python/Dockerfile; file_abs_path says it is in resource-managers/kubernetes/core/pom.xml, and repo_file_path, which would ordinarily arbitrate, is null. The two name different files in different directories, one a Dockerfile and one a Maven pom, and both files really exist at the pin -- so neither can be dismissed as obviously the corrupt one. AAP 0.1.3 forbids picking one: a record that cannot be attributed with certainty is rejected and the rejection recorded as a class with its count, never guessed into a field. The record is therefore counted under unresolvable_path with the reason retained, and no path is supplied for it anywhere in this file.
rejection_boundary.the_contradiction_is_also_unexpressible: The same record fails for a second, independent reason, and both are recorded because either alone would suffice. The anchor value is the URI file:///opt/spark-src/resource-managers/kubernetes/core/pom.xml, and paths.assert_relative_path refuses any value carrying a scheme in _EMITTED_PATH_FORBIDDEN_SCHEMES -- 'file' among them -- so even a reader willing to prefer the anchor over file_path could not emit what it names. That is why the recorded detail speaks of the URI scheme: the resolver reaches the unexpressible-anchor guard before the recorded disagreement can be attached to a row. The disagreement is the substantive fault and the scheme is the mechanism by which it surfaces; a fixture whose anchor merely disagreed while remaining expressible would produce a kept row with the disagreement recorded, which is a different behaviour with its own coverage note below.
rejection_boundary.the_second_rejection: /results/failed_checks/3 is the other sub-reason the same class covers, and it is not a duplicate of the first. That record carries no anchor at all -- repo_file_path and file_abs_path are both null -- leaving only a file_path the runner metadata records as relative to whichever of 18 -d target roots the record came from. Without an anchor there is no way to know which target that was, and the scan root is not a substitute for the answer: joining the stripped value to the root would name dockerfiles/spark/bindings/R/Dockerfile, which exists nowhere in the tree and matches no allowlist glob, so the row would carry a wrong path and a wrong in_scope with nothing failing. It is not absent_path either, because the record does name a location; it names one that cannot be anchored.
rejection_boundary.pairing_with_the_positive_fixture: The pairing is the point of the pair. oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/checkov.rows.json proves the leading slash is honoured: five records whose consistent triples all resolve, with path_corroboration_recorded 0. This file proves the file_abs_path reconciliation is a real check rather than decoration -- and it is reliable precisely because the runner passes one -d per expanded absolute directory, which is what makes file_path target-relative and an anchor field the only thing that can place a record in the tree. Read together, the two files establish that the adapter honours the convention and still refuses a record the convention cannot place. Either file alone would leave the other half unproven.

mechanisms_not_used.mechanism: a leading slash on file_path treated as the fault
mechanisms_not_used.why_not: A leading slash on file_path is correct Checkov convention -- it is the user's own worked example -- and treating it as a defect would encode a bug into this suite and contradict the example it exists to carry. Every record in this fixture, the two rows included, carries a leading slash on file_path, and none is rejected for it.

AAP 0.8.3 makes those kept rows with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope. Out of scope means kept and marked, never rejected: only evidence about the runner establishes a wrong scan root, and an individual coordinate outside the twelve globs is a legitimate coordinate. Rejecting one here would assert the opposite of what the AAP requires.

rejection_boundary.fault_verified_from_the_fixture: Checked rather than assumed, in both directions. Each defective record differs from its captured original in exactly its two anchor fields and in nothing else -- 26 of 28 fields identical by canonical comparison -- so the fault cannot be anything but the path. And neither defective record trips an earlier classification step: each is a JSON object, each carries a non-empty check_id, and each carries a non-empty check_name, so steps 1 to 3 all pass and the path is the only thing left to reject them for.

not_a_rejection.case: a path resolving outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: This runner legitimately reaches such coordinates, since its reach is shaped by its 18 -d roots while in_scope is the allowlist's answer and not the runner's.

not_a_rejection.case: an anchor disagreement that is nonetheless expressible
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row on the first anchor in the recorded order, with the disagreement recorded in the resolution's corroboration and counted under path_corroboration_recorded
not_a_rejection.evidence: paths.resolve_checkov_path reconciles the anchors against each other and records a mismatch rather than resolving it, and the corroboration never suppresses a row. This fixture's first defective record carries a disagreement, but its anchor is a file: URI, so it is refused before any row exists to record the note on -- which is why path_corroboration_recorded is 0 below and not 1.

not_a_rejection.case: a path in a src/test tree
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false
not_a_rejection.evidence: The exclusion is literal -- a path containing src/test is out of scope -- and it removes the path from scope rather than from the dataset.

not_a_rejection.case: a passed check, a skipped check or a parsing error
not_a_rejection.evidence: See failures_only below. A parsing error in particular is Checkov's own report about a file it could not read, not a finding this adapter could not attribute; converting one into a rejection would put it on the right-hand side of the identity while the independent traversal never put it on the left.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_path: Neither rejected record is given a path. Nothing in this file supplies a coordinate for either one, not even a plausible one -- and for the first record the plausible candidates are exactly what is being refused.

failures_only.count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[], the union across every report object in either top-level shape
failures_only.passed_checks_note: Neither counted nor emitted, and neither check_id may appear anywhere in the rows array. Both pass on resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile because line 71 of that file is USER ${spark_uid} -- the last instruction, and not root. CKV_DOCKER_3 in particular is the check the same file's CKV_DOCKER_2 failure sits beside, so a bucket-blind adapter would emit a row for a check that genuinely passed. They are observable only through the passed_checks_observed counter, which is what makes produced-no-row an observation rather than a claim.
failures_only.skipped_checks_note: Neither counted nor emitted, exactly as passed checks are not. The one entry is CKV_DOCKER_9 on bindings/R/Dockerfile at file_line_range [34, 37] carrying a suppress_comment, and it must produce no row even though the identical check_id on the main Dockerfile does -- the bucket decides that, never the check_id. It is also the only record in this fixture that names bindings/R/Dockerfile with usable anchors, and it must not be read as supplying the anchor the failed check on that same file is missing: attribution is per record, and borrowing a field from a neighbouring record is the inference AAP 0.1.3 forbids.
failures_only.parsing_errors_note: Status evidence for oss-scan-results/tool-status.md, carried verbatim, and neither a finding nor a rejection. The distinction matters more in this fixture than in the positive one, because this document does contain rejections: a reader could reasonably expect the parsing error to join them. It must not. A rejection describes a failed check this adapter could not attribute; a parsing error is the tool's report about a file it never turned into a check, and it is not one of the counted failed checks. Counting it would make rejections 3 while the independent traversal still returned 4, breaking the identity for something that was never a finding. The named file exists at the pin: it is a shell script the dockerfile framework does not parse.
failures_only.vacuity_note: The three zero expectations above are why this fixture carries non-empty passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors at all. Against an artifact whose buckets were empty -- which is what the raw artifact's --compact output is -- the failures-only contract would be satisfied by an adapter that read every bucket, and the assertion would prove nothing.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of results.failed_checks[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("checkov", doc), whose traversal reduces both top-level shapes to a sequence of report objects and sums the length of each results.failed_checks array, building no row, resolving no path and mapping no severity. It reads reconcile.CHECKOV_COUNTED_SECTION and nothing else, so passed_checks, skipped_checks and parsing_errors contribute zero by construction. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing.
counts.rejection_class_count_note: One class, two records under it. The two are not a duplicated case: they are the two distinct sub-reasons paths.py names for this class on this tool -- an anchor that cannot be expressed against the root, and no anchor at all under per_target_directory -- and each is reached by a different code path. Recording them separately under one class is exactly what AAP 0.5.4 asks of a class that covers several routes: the class carries the count, the detail carries which route it was.
counts.reconciliation_status_authority: normalize.reconcile, STATUS_PASS = "pass". Its STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE and the verdict reconcile.NOT_APPLICABLE_ABSENT are for a tool that wrote no artifact and are not in play here: this artifact exists and carries records.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason each of the four is zero.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and both rejected records are counted under their class, with their reasons retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse -- and note that the two co-exist here: the parse is partial while the reconciliation assertion passes.
counts.row_count_note: 2 is not len(results.failed_checks): it is that length minus the two rejected records. Two passed checks, one skipped check and one parsing error sit in the same document, and any one of them leaking in would make this 3, 4, 5 or 6, while a rejected record silently coerced into a row would make it 3 or 4 with the identity still balancing -- which is why the rejections array below is asserted by class and detail rather than by count alone.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/checkov.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): nineteen authored keys, one path_kind_* per member of normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS and one severity_basis_* per member of normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES -- twenty-eight in all, every one an int.
counters_note: Four values a reader must not 'correct'. First, path_corroboration_recorded is 0, not 1, even though /results/failed_checks/2 does carry a file_path that disagrees with its anchor: the counter is incremented from a resolution that came back, and that record's resolution never came back, because constructing it raised on the anchor's URI scheme. The disagreement is reported in the rejection's detail instead, which is where a record with no row has to report anything. Second, every severity and path_kind counter is 2 rather than 4: severity is step 6 of the record walk and the path is step 4, so neither rejected record ever reaches a severity or contributes a path kind, and there is deliberately no adapter-side count of records walked, rows or rejections -- those are returned to the caller directly, and the independent left-hand side of the identity is normalize.reconcile.count_records. Third, start_line_absent is 0 because both rows carry a usable file_line_range; the two rejected records also carry one and are never asked for it. Fourth, the four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool are all 0: caller_file_path is null on every record so none names a second location, no record carries a CWE or CVE identifier in the closed source field set, and both emitted paths name a file inside the scanned tree.
counters_root_note: Given some other absolute scan root, no counter above changes and no row changes. Both rows take their path from repo_file_path, which needs no root; both rejections are root-independent, the first because a file: URI is unexpressible under any root and the second because a missing anchor is supplied by no root. The positive sibling's path_corroboration_recorded is root-dependent because its records carry two resolvable anchors that would disagree under a different root; here the only record with a second anchor is rejected before any note can be recorded, so even that dependency is absent.

recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.resolution: The fixture governs, because this file is the expected result *for that fixture*. Both defective records classify under unresolvable_path, so the brief's class is exactly right and only the count differs; the brief was evidently written against a fixture carrying one defective record, and the fixture as committed carries two. Recording the difference with both values rather than picking one silently is AAP 0.9.3's rule for an observed difference from an expectation.
recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.why_not_written_as_one: The two alternatives are both worse than a recorded difference. Emitting a row for /results/failed_checks/3 to make rejections 1 would supply a path the record cannot support -- the guess AAP 0.1.3 forbids, and one paths.resolve_checkov_path refuses by contract, so the expectation would contradict the adapter it describes. Dropping that record instead would break the identity, since normalize.reconcile.count_records independently counts 4. Neither is available, and neither should be.
recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.fixture_not_edited: The fixture is not trimmed to match the brief. It is another deliverable with its own provenance, its two defective records exercise both sub-reasons of the class rather than one, and editing a fixture so a document's number comes out right is the inversion this suite exists to prevent -- expectations are re-derived when a fixture changes, never the other way round.

recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.field: the emitted path's relationship to file_path
recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.brief_states: each row's path equals its record's file_path minus the leading slash
recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.fixture_yields: each row's path is the anchored path -- repo_file_path minus exactly one leading slash -- of which the stripped file_path is a proper suffix
recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.resolution: The authored contract governs, and it is the same contract the already-committed positive sibling records. Under the recorded path_base.kind per_target_directory the stripped file_path is relative to whichever of 18 -d roots matched, so it cannot be the row's path: dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile names no location at the root. AAP 0.5.4's generic checkov row -- path from file_path with its leading slash stripped, reconciled against file_abs_path -- describes the single-target shape; runner-metadata.json records the shape this provisioning actually invoked, and the AAP requires that metadata be read as input rather than assumed. Both readings are stated here so the difference is visible.
recorded_divergences_from_the_authoring_.assertion_that_holds_instead: For every row: the path carries no leading slash and no ../ segment, the stripped file_path is a suffix of it, and the relativized file_abs_path equals it exactly. That is strictly stronger than the brief's equality, and it is what row_derivations records per row under path_cross_check and file_path_is_suffix_of_anchored_path.

corroboration.note: The two surviving records are captured output that already appears elsewhere, so both rows can be corroborated rather than only asserted. Row 0 here is the positive sibling's row 4 and row 1 is its row 3, all twenty-four field comparisons agreeing; and the committed dataset carries both -- CKV_DOCKER_2 at start_line 1 and CKV_DOCKER_9 at start_line 36, each on resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile. Recorded after the fact rather than as the source of these values: each was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply. The two rejected records have no counterpart to corroborate against -- they are this fixture's own synthesized additions, appear in no captured artifact, and contribute no dataset row.
corroboration.dataset_rows_not_expected_here: The committed dataset carries six checkov rows; four of them come from records this fixture either replaced with a defective variant or never included, so their absence from these rows is the fixture's derivation holding rather than a discrepancy.

rows.message: Ensure that HEALTHCHECK instructions have been added to container images

row_derivations.bc_check_id_note: null here, and never a fallback for check_id in any case: AAP 0.5.4 names check_id as the source of rule_id.
row_derivations.severity_native_note: null in the record, because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is absent; the absence is stated rather than a level assumed
row_derivations.path_transform: exactly one leading slash stripped; the remainder is already root-relative
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: every field in the closed identifier source set is null or an empty array on this record, so no CWE token exists to collect
row_derivations.glob_match_note: the mid-path ** absorbs the single segment docker, and the trailing ** absorbs dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile -- zero-or-more-directories semantics, which fnmatch and PurePath.match do not provide
row_derivations.pin_evidence: A whole-file check whose range [1, 71] spans the file exactly. Verified at the pinned commit: the file is exactly 71 lines and contains zero HEALTHCHECK instructions, so CKV_DOCKER_2 genuinely fails and this row is a real finding rather than a fixture artefact. Line 71 is USER ${spark_uid}, which is why CKV_DOCKER_3 and CKV_DOCKER_8 genuinely pass on the same file and produce no row. start_line 1 is within the file, and no start_line anywhere in this file exceeds 71.

row_derivations.bc_check_id_note: null here, and never a fallback for check_id in any case: AAP 0.5.4 names check_id as the source of rule_id.
row_derivations.message_note: check_name exactly as the record carries it, apostrophe included. Nothing is assembled from check_id, guideline, resource or code_block, and no content from check_result.results_configuration reaches any field -- that record quotes a multi-line RUN instruction including shell redirection, and none of it is emitted.
row_derivations.severity_native_note: null in the record, because severities require a licence and BC_API_KEY is absent; the absence is stated rather than a level assumed
row_derivations.path_transform: exactly one leading slash stripped; the remainder is already root-relative
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: every field in the closed identifier source set is null or an empty array on this record, so no CWE token exists to collect
row_derivations.glob_match_note: the mid-path ** absorbs the single segment docker, and the trailing ** absorbs dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile -- zero-or-more-directories semantics, which fnmatch and PurePath.match do not provide
row_derivations.pin_evidence: Verified at the pinned commit: line 36 of the 71-line file is RUN set -ex && \, the opening line of the apt-installing RUN instruction this record quotes, so start_line 36 names the instruction it claims and is within the file. The same file's CKV_DOCKER_9 on bindings/R/Dockerfile sits in skipped_checks in this fixture and produces no row, which is the bucket deciding the outcome rather than the check_id.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and the report_index / check_index pair name the same record. The pair is carried as well because normalize.adapters.checkov passes exactly report_index, check_index, check_type and check_id into the rejection it builds, so a produced Rejection's record_identity and this expectation can be compared directly, without translating one coordinate system into the other.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 all pass on this record: it is a JSON object, it carries check_id CKV_DOCKER_2, and it carries a non-empty check_name. That is deliberate, so the only thing left to reject it for is its path.
rejections.start_line_never_examined: Step 5 is never reached, so this record's file_line_range of [1, 46] is never examined and non_integer_start_line is not in play. Worth stating because the fixture does give the defective record a usable range, and a reader could otherwise expect an interaction between the two conditions.
rejections.produced_by: paths.PathPolicyError raised inside paths.resolve_checkov_path and caught by the adapter, which converts it to a counted rejection rather than letting it discard the whole artifact. RunnerMetadataError is caught first and re-raised, being a subclass -- a metadata fault is a caller fault, not a defective record.
rejections.normalisation_note: paths.normalise_reported_path drops empty interior segments, so the URI's // authority separator collapses and the value reaches assert_relative_path as a scheme-bearing reference rather than as a // authority. Either shape is refused; this is the one that actually occurs, and the recorded detail quotes it.
rejections.why_unresolvable: Two independent reasons, both true of this record. The anchor cannot be expressed against the scan root at all: paths.assert_relative_path refuses a value carrying a URI scheme in _EMITTED_PATH_FORBIDDEN_SCHEMES, and file is one of them, so no emitted path can be formed from it and ResolvedPath cannot even be constructed. And the record's two statements about its location contradict each other -- file_path names a Dockerfile under dockerfiles/spark/bindings/python while file_abs_path names resource-managers/kubernetes/core/pom.xml, a different real file in a different directory -- with repo_file_path null, so nothing arbitrates. file_path cannot be promoted to fill the gap either, because under per_target_directory it is relative to whichever of 18 -d roots matched and the scan root is not a substitute for that answer.
rejections.expected_detail: the failed check's path fields cannot be expressed against the scan root: 'file:/opt/spark-src/resource-managers/kubernetes/core/pom.xml' carries the URI scheme 'file', not a path relative to the root
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, and it is quoted here because this class covers several routes: naming the class alone would not distinguish this record from the next rejection, which is the same class for a different reason. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings -- 'cannot be expressed against the scan root' and "URI scheme 'file'" -- rather than by full-string equality, since the detail is prose that quotes the record's own value.
rejections.record_identity_note: These four keys are the adapter's own, supplied at the point it catches the error, which is why this identity differs in shape from the next rejection's. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no path to put in the row. path is never absent from a row, so a record whose coordinate cannot be expressed has no valid row representation, and the alternatives -- dropping it, or giving it one of its two contradictory candidates -- would each hide it. Counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejections.why_not_a_recorded_corroboration: A disagreement between a record's path fields is ordinarily recorded on the row and counted under path_corroboration_recorded, never rejected. That route needs a row to record the note on, and this record cannot produce one, because the anchor the note would qualify is itself unexpressible. So the disagreement is reported in the detail instead, and path_corroboration_recorded stays 0.
rejections.why_not_invalid_uri: invalid_uri is for an entry whose URI is syntactically invalid. This one is syntactically valid: it parses cleanly as a file: URI and names a file that exists at the pin. What disqualifies it is that a valid URI is not a path relative to the root, which is the unresolvable_path case.
rejections.why_not_absent_path: absent_path is for a record that carries no path field or an empty one. This record carries two.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so no native literal from it reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none. Its severity is null in any case, which is exactly what makes the omission easy to miss and worth stating.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and the pair name the same record. Unlike the first rejection, this one's record_identity does not carry the pair: paths.resolve_checkov_path builds the Rejection itself from the record's own fields and the adapter returns it as-is, deliberately, so the class and sub-reason paths.py named are not reworded on the way out. The asymmetry is authored rather than accidental and a test must expect it.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH constant -- the same literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES as the rejection above, reached by a different route.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order. Steps 1 to 3 pass on this record too: it is an object, it carries check_id CKV_DOCKER_2, and it carries a non-empty check_name.
rejections.start_line_never_examined: Step 5 is never reached, so this record's file_line_range of [1, 47] is never examined.
rejections.produced_by: returned directly by paths.resolve_checkov_path, which reaches its final branch: no anchor field yielded a value, a file_path corroborator is present, and the recorded path_base.kind is per_target_directory rather than scan_root.
rejections.why_unresolvable: The record names a location, but not one that can be placed in the tree. Its only path field is a file_path the runner metadata records as relative to whichever of the runner's 18 -d target roots the record came from, and with both anchors null there is no way to know which that was. Joining the stripped value to the scan root would name dockerfiles/spark/bindings/R/Dockerfile, which exists nowhere at the pin and matches no allowlist glob, so the row would carry a wrong path and in_scope false with nothing failing -- the silent failure the worked example warns about, arrived at from the other direction. The scan root is not a substitute for the answer.
rejections.expected_detail: the failed check carries only file_path ('/dockerfiles/spark/bindings/R/Dockerfile'), which the runner metadata records as relative to whichever of the runner's targets the record came from (path_base.kind 'per_target_directory', anchor fields repo_file_path, file_abs_path). Without an anchor field there is no way to know which target that was, and the scan root is not a substitute for the answer
rejections.expected_detail_note: Quoted for the same reason as the first rejection's: the class is shared and only the detail distinguishes the route. Distinguishing substrings are 'carries only file_path' and 'the scan root is not a substitute for the answer'.
rejections.record_identity_note: paths.resolve_checkov_path builds the identity from check_id, file_path and repo_file_path, omitting any of the three that is null -- so repo_file_path is absent from it here. The raw file_path is carried verbatim, leading slash included, because the identity records what the record said rather than what the resolver made of it.
rejections.why_not_a_row: Same reason as above: there is no path to put in the row, and the one candidate present cannot be anchored. A row would have to invent the target directory the record failed to name.
rejections.why_not_absent_path: absent_path is the sibling class for a record that names no location at all -- both anchors and file_path absent or empty. This record does name one; it names one that cannot be anchored. Distinguishing the two is why both classes exist, and why an adapter test asserts the class name rather than merely counting rejections.
rejections.not_resolved_from_a_neighbouring_record: The skipped check in this same report names bindings/R/Dockerfile with both anchors intact, and the positive fixture carries a failed check on that file with both anchors intact. Neither may supply this record's missing anchor: attribution is per record, and borrowing a field from a neighbour is precisely the inference AAP 0.1.3 forbids. That the correct path is knowable from elsewhere in the document is what makes this the sharper of the two rejections.
rejections.if_the_base_kind_were_scan_root: Recorded because it is the one thing that would change this outcome, and it is a property of the provisioning rather than of the record. Had the runner passed a single -d equal to the scan root, the recorded path_base.kind would be scan_root, the stripped file_path would really be root-relative, and this record would become a kept row with the basis checkov-file-path-leading-slash-stripped. It did not: runner-metadata.json records 18 -d roots in one invocation. The expectation follows the recorded metadata, not the shape a reader might assume.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: Never fed to the severity tally, so no literal from it reaches severity-map.md.

scope_of_this_file.records_only_this_tool: These are checkov's rows and rejections and nothing else. Trivy also reports misconfigurations on the same Dockerfile, and that produces trivy's own rows in trivy's own expected file: no comparison, no deduplication, no ranking and no cross-tool interpretation is made here, and nothing in this file characterises a finding as real, important or a false positive. Two tools reporting the same location produce two rows and no comment.
scope_of_this_file.no_secret_value: No field carries a secret or any content from check_result.results_configuration. message is check_name and nothing else, so the multi-line shell text those records quote -- including the apt invocations and the pam.d redirection -- reaches no row and no rejection detail. The absolute paths that appear are quoted evidence about the fixture, never emitted data. This tree is committed to git.
scope_of_this_file.no_inference: A record whose path could not be established with certainty is a counted rejection, never a path picked from two candidates. This file is where that rule is exercised for checkov, and the rule is why it carries two rejections rather than one row and one rejection.
scope_of_this_file.no_judgement_of_the_findings: That the anchor Dockerfile has no HEALTHCHECK is recorded as the reason CKV_DOCKER_2 fires and therefore as evidence the row is real tool output. It is not a claim that the finding matters, and no remediation is suggested anywhere.
